question.text: Under FEMA, which of the following is an example of a 'current account transaction'?

answer.text: External commercial borrowing by an Indian company
Foreign direct investment in an Indian company
Import and export of goods and services

explanation.text: The Logic: Under FEMA, import and export of goods and services are current account transactions, while FDI, portfolio investment by FPIs and external commercial borrowing alter assets or liabilities and are therefore capital account transactions. The Trap: FDI, FPI portfolio investment and ECB all change the cross-border asset/liability position of an Indian entity, so they are capital account transactions, not current account. Note: Capital account transactions alter assets or liabilities and are governed by FEMA/RBI rules, with approval requirements depending on the route or instrument (for example, page 212 describes Automatic Route FDI with no RBI/Government approval).
